stories.title: Coin Metrics fetcher — MVRV, BTC only, rate-limit handling proven against real data
stories.description:
As the owner, I want BTC's MVRV fetched from Coin Metrics' free Community API with its rate
limit respected, so that this project's first non-OKX vendor integration establishes the
pattern correctly before four more registry entries build on it.

Coin Metrics' Community tier needs no API key and returns simple, string-typed JSON —
`{"data": [{"asset": "btc", "time": "...", "CapMVRVCur": "..."}]}` — but is rate-limited to
roughly 10 requests per 6-second sliding window **per IP**, not per key. A naive concurrent
batch at the start of a scheduled run will 429; a naive sequential one with no backoff will
429 anyway once the on-chain panel's full metric set is registered. This story proves the
client respects that limit against the real endpoint before any other story reuses it.

criteria.text: Community tier is genuinely key-free; sending one anyway would be a silent, undocumented assumption

method.name: the fetcher calls `/v4/timeseries/asset-metrics` with `assets=btc&metrics=CapMVRVCur`, no API key header or query param present

criteria.text: The fetcher never interprets an error body as data

method.name: a `bad_parameter` error response returns Error(FETCH_FAILED) with the message in the detail, never a value

criteria.text: Coin Metrics' own vocabulary for "exists, we lack credentials" maps directly onto this project's `PAYWALLED` reason — proven against the real `CapRealUSD` endpoint, which is confirmed forbidden on the free tier

method.name: a `forbidden` error response (a credential-gated metric) returns Unavailable(PAYWALLED), distinct from FETCH_FAILED

criteria.text: `extra="forbid"` on the new `CoinMetricsAssetMetricsResponse` — an added, renamed, or retyped field fails loud

method.name: a malformed or reshaped response is rejected by the response model

criteria.text: A burst of calls at run start must not 429 the whole batch; prove it with more than one call in the same test, not a single request that happens to succeed once

method.name: consecutive requests within one run are serialized with backoff sufficient to stay under ~1.6 req/s

criteria.text: Same discipline as every fetcher in this project

method.name: an HTTP error returns Error with the status code in the detail, and no value

criteria.text: The F11 defence

method.name: source_timestamp is the response's own `time` field and is strictly in the past

criteria.text: Hits the real endpoint; this is what actually pins the response shape, since Coin Metrics' full field vocabulary was not exhaustively catalogued in research

method.name: a live request returns BTC's current MVRV

criteria.text: Strict typing holds for the new module

# crypto-data-live-platform

<!--
Written by a person, kept short. Generated agent instructions measurably do not help —
they cost tokens on every invocation and slightly reduce success rates, while
human-written context improves them. When an agent learns something worth keeping it
writes a proposal to `.uf/proposals/`; you fold in the ones that are actually true.

An empty section is better than an invented one.
-->

**Stack:** Python 3.12 (`uv`, httpx, pydantic, TA-Lib) ingestion · Supabase Postgres ·
Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind on Cloudflare Pages, behind Cloudflare Access ·
GitHub Actions `schedule:` + cron-job.org `repository_dispatch` triggers ·
Healthchecks.io dead-man's-switch.
See `project-documents/10_Technical_Architecture.md`.

> **Compute location is UNDECIDED** until PRD-001's reachability spike runs. Binance returns
> HTTP 451 to US IPs, which is what forced the prior system onto a self-hosted runner that
> later died silently. Do not assume GitHub-hosted runners can reach every venue — measure it.

**This product's one rule above all others:** it displays market data and **makes no
judgement about it**. No composite score, no signal, no ranking. A wrong number must look
different from a right one — that is the whole product. If a value cannot be honestly sourced
for an asset, it renders `UNAVAILABLE` with a reason, never a proxy and never `0`.

## How work happens here

This product runs on `uf`. Read `CYCLE.md` for the loop, `SKILLS.md` for which skill to fire
at which phase, `KNOWLEDGE.md` for what we already know.

Work is organised as **PRDs** in `prds/PRD-00N-<slug>/`, walked in the order set by
`project-documents/05_Product_Roadmap.md`. Each PRD compiles to `spec.lock.json`, then runs
story by story: one agent implements in a fresh context, a **different vendor** verifies in
a read-only sandbox and must cite a file, line or test name per criterion.

**You cannot mark your own work complete.** Produce the evidence the criteria name — the
tests, the screenshots, the passing commands — and leave it where it can be found. Do not
write a summary claiming success; nobody reads it and the verifier ignores it.

## Conventions

<!-- Add the real ones as you discover them. -->

## Gotchas

<!-- Things that cost an afternoon. Also run `uf learn` so other products inherit them. -->

## Blast radius

Changes to these need human review before merge (mirrored in `.uf/config.json`):

- authentication and session handling
- RLS policies
- payments
- database migrations
- CI workflows and deploy configuration

## What we already knew, and whether it still holds

| Claim from our knowledge base | Still true? | What the source says | Citation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coin Metrics free Community API needs no API key | **Confirmed** | Community endpoints at `api.coinmetrics.io/v4` require no key | [gitbook-docs.coinmetrics.io/access-our-data/api](https://gitbook-docs.coinmetrics.io/access-our-data/api), confirmed on [coin-metrics-community-data](https://gitbook-docs.coinmetrics.io/packages/coin-metrics-community-data) |
| R2's live probe found BTC/ETH MVRV, active addresses, exchange flows FREE; SOL MVRV/exchange-flows NO-METRIC | Holds — not contradicted by anything fetched | No public source disputes R2's live probe; Coin Metrics' own coverage explorer is the only way to re-verify, and it requires a live query per asset/metric, which is what R2 already did | Not independently re-verified here — see Open Questions |
| "Coin Metrics API key provisioning and rate limits... need confirming" (brief's open question) | **Now answered** | Community tier: **10 requests / 6-second sliding window per IP (~1.6 req/s)**, no key required | [coinmetrics.readthedocs.io/en/latest/community.html](https://coinmetrics.readthedocs.io/en/latest/community.html) via search, corroborated by [gitbook-docs.coinmetrics.io/access-our-data/api](https://gitbook-docs.coinmetrics.io/access-our-data/api) |
| "BNB coverage is asserted in the roadmap but not independently confirmed" (brief's open question) | **Still unconfirmed** | Neither Coin Metrics doc fetched lists per-asset metric coverage inline; the actual answer lives behind a live query to `coverage.coinmetrics.io` or the `/v4/catalog-all/asset-metrics` endpoint, which this research pass did not execute against BNB specifically | [gitbook-docs.coinmetrics.io/network-data/network-data-overview/addresses/active-addresses](https://gitbook-docs.coinmetrics.io/network-data/network-data-overview/addresses/active-addresses) confirms only that privacy coins (Monero, Grin) are excluded — silent on BNB either way |
| R8: "Vote vs. non-vote transaction filtering on Solana... could not reconfirm the current vote/non-vote split live" | **R8 was right to flag this — and the answer is worse than "unconfirmed": it's unsupported** | `getBlock`'s only config params are `commitment`, `encoding`, `transactionDetails`, `maxSupportedTransactionVersion`, `rewards` — **no vote-filter parameter exists**. A 2022 feature request to add one (`votes: bool`) was explicitly closed as **not planned** | [solana.com/docs/rpc/http/getblock](https://solana.com/docs/rpc/http/getblock); [github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/29856](https://github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/29856) (closed, not planned; repo itself now archived) |
| R8: Validators.app "confirmed genuinely free, no paid tier exists at all" | **Holds, but with a real constraint not previously recorded** | No paid tier is documented, but the free API is rate-limited to **20 or 40 requests per 5 minutes depending on endpoint**, requires a verified account + token, and returns 429 on overage | [validators.app/api-documentation](https://www.validators.app/api-documentation) |
| R8: Helius/QuickNode "both confirmed free tiers... neither was load-tested" | **Partially updated** | Helius free tier: **1M monthly credits, 10 req/s** overall cap, with tighter per-method sub-limits (1 `sendTransaction`/s, 2 DAS calls/s, 5 `getProgramAccounts`/s) — this project's read-only daily batch (getBlock/getSignaturesForAddress calls) fits comfortably under 10 req/s if paced | [helius.dev/docs/billing/rate-limits](https://www.helius.dev/docs/billing/rate-limits) |

## Existing implementations

Real dashboards separate the exact three metric classes this PRD does:

- **The Block** and **Token Terminal** both publish "Non-vote transactions on Solana" as a distinct series from raw transaction count, precisely because raw counts are consensus noise, not user activity — both are downstream evidence that shipped implementations treat vote-filtering as necessary, even though the raw RPC gives no server-side lever for it: [theblock.co/data/on-chain-metrics/solana/non-vote-transactions-on-the-solana-network-daily-7dma](https://www.theblock.co/data/on-chain-metrics/solana/non-vote-transactions-on-the-solana-network-daily-7dma), [tokenterminal.com/explorer/projects/solana/metrics/non-vote-transaction-count](https://tokenterminal.com/explorer/projects/solana/metrics/non-vote-transaction-count).
- **Solscan's own analytics dashboard** exposes "vote vs non-vote transactions" as a first-class split view, again implying client-side classification against fetched blocks rather than a filtered RPC call: [analytics.solscan.io/overview/transaction/vote-vs-non-vote-trans](https://analytics.solscan.io/overview/transaction/vote-vs-non-vote-trans).
- **UNVERIFIED** (own recall, not confirmed by a fetched source this pass): the standard client-side technique is to inspect each transaction's account keys / program invocations for the vote program address `Vote111111111111111111111111111111111111111` and classify a transaction as a vote iff every top-level instruction targets that program. This needs direct confirmation against Solana's program docs or a working reference implementation before it becomes a story's acceptance criterion — flagged as a research gap below, not a settled fact.
- **Coin Metrics' own Python/R clients** (`coinmetrics-api-client`) wrap the same public `/v4` community endpoints this PRD would call directly via httpx — evidence the free tier is treated as production-usable by Coin Metrics itself, not a crippled trial: [github.com/coinmetrics/docs-website](https://github.com/coinmetrics/docs-website).

## Approach options

**1. Coin Metrics Community API, direct httpx, for BTC/ETH (and BNB if confirmed) — recommended for the on-chain fetch.**
How: daily batch call to `/v4/timeseries/asset-metrics` for `CapMVRVCur`, `AdrActCnt`, exchange-flow metrics, one asset per call to respect the ~1.6 req/s ceiling. Cost: $0. Trade-off: rate limit means a 4-asset × 3-metric daily batch (12 calls) takes ~7+ seconds minimum if serialized correctly — trivial for a once-daily job, but a naive concurrent implementation will get 429'd. Who uses it: Coin Metrics' own community client library is built on exactly this endpoint set ([github.com/coinmetrics/docs-website](https://github.com/coinmetrics/docs-website)).

**2. Helius free-tier RPC for SOL network activity — recommended for the build side.**
How: `getBlock` per slot (or `getSignaturesForAddress`/batch RPC) at a sampled cadence, client-side vote-filtering, aggregated to daily non-vote tx count + unique signers. Cost: $0 within 1M credits/mo, 10 req/s ceiling ([helius.dev/docs/billing/rate-limits](https://www.helius.dev/docs/billing/rate-limits)). Trade-off: no server-side vote filter exists at all ([github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/29856](https://github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/29856)) — every block's full transaction list must be pulled and filtered locally, which is real client-side compute and credit cost, not "free" in the way R8 characterized it.

**3. QuickNode free tier as the Solana RPC alternative.**
How: same interface as Helius, different provider. Trade-off: R8 did not load-test either against this project's real batch shape, and this research pass did not re-test it either — this remains a genuine open decision, not a settled one. Cost: $0 documented free tier exists, per [quicknode.com/builders-guide/best/top-10-free-rpc-endpoints-for-developers](https://www.quicknode.com/builders-guide/best/top-10-free-rpc-endpoints-for-developers).

**4. Validators.app for SOL staking/validator data — recommended, only option researched with a confirmed no-paid-tier posture.**
How: token-gated GET requests against their REST API for validator count, commission, active stake. Cost: $0, but capped at 20–40 requests/5 min depending on endpoint, with a mandatory account + API token, not a fully anonymous free tier ([validators.app/api-documentation](https://www.validators.app/api-documentation)) — a materially stricter free tier than Coin Metrics' anonymous-by-IP model.

**Recommendation:** Coin Metrics Community API (option 1) for BTC/ETH/BNB-if-confirmed, Helius free tier (option 2) for SOL network activity, Validators.app (option 4) for SOL staking. This matches R8's build-don't-buy verdict and every number above is now sourced rather than catalog-asserted — one line of justification: **it's the only combination where every claimed "free" limit has a live-fetched number attached to it (rate limit, credit cap, or req/5min cap), not a vendor marketing page.**

## Edge cases and gotchas

- **The vote-filter gotcha is worse than "unconfirmed" — it's a myth to retire.** R8 phrased this as "a filtering problem, not a scale-blocking problem," implying some RPC-level knob exists to flip. It doesn't: `getBlock` has never supported vote exclusion, and the 2022 feature request for it was explicitly rejected ([github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/29856](https://github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/29856)). Any story that says "confirm the RPC-level filter works as documented" is testing something that was never documented to exist. The story needs to specify client-side vote-program-instruction classification instead, and that classification logic itself needs a cited reference before being written into an acceptance criterion — currently it is only this document's UNVERIFIED recall.
- **Coin Metrics' rate limit is per-IP, not per-key** — a GitHub Actions runner's ephemeral IP means the limit resets cleanly run-to-run, but also means it cannot be "banked" or monitored via a dashboard; a burst of concurrent asset/metric calls at the start of a batch job will 429 silently unless serialized with backoff (10 req/6s ≈ 1.6 req/s — [coinmetrics.readthedocs.io/en/latest/community.html](https://coinmetrics.readthedocs.io/en/latest/community.html)).
- **Validators.app requires a verified account and per-endpoint rate ceilings** — this is a materially different trust/provisioning model than Coin Metrics' anonymous-by-IP approach, and the brief's framing of R8's "confirmed genuinely free" undersold the friction: a token must be provisioned and stored as a secret before US-0xx work can even start ([validators.app/api-documentation](https://www.validators.app/api-documentation)).
- **Helius free-tier per-method sub-caps can bite even under the 10 req/s headline number** — `getProgramAccounts` is capped at 5/s and DAS calls at 2/s regardless of the 10 req/s overall ceiling; if the SOL story ends up needing `getProgramAccounts` for anything (e.g. enumerating stake accounts as a cross-check against Validators.app), that path is throttled tighter than the naive "10 req/s, fine" read of the plan ([helius.dev/docs/billing/rate-limits](https://www.helius.dev/docs/billing/rate-limits)).
- **BNB coverage is still an assumption, not a fact, after this research pass.** Neither fetched Coin Metrics page lists per-asset metric availability; the only way to settle it per the brief's own instruction is a live, one-metric-at-a-time probe against `/v4/timeseries/asset-metrics?assets=bnb&metrics=CapMVRVCur` etc. — this document did not execute that probe and it must happen before `20-decisions.yaml` is written, or BNB coverage remains catalog-asserted exactly as R2 originally warned against for SOL.

## Services and keys this PRD needs

| Service | Why | Env var | Already provisioned? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coin Metrics Community API | BTC/ETH (and BNB, pending confirmation) MVRV, active addresses, exchange flows | none required (no key) | N/A — no provisioning needed |
| Helius (or QuickNode) Solana RPC, free tier | SOL block/transaction fetch for network-activity build | `HELIUS_API_KEY` (or `QUICKNODE_URL`) | **Unconfirmed** — not verified in this repo's existing secrets; owner must sign up |
| Validators.app API | SOL staking/validator data | `VALIDATORS_APP_API_TOKEN` | **Unconfirmed** — requires a verified account, not yet provisioned |

## Open questions for the human

| Question | My hypothesis | Impact if wrong |
|---|---|---|
| Does Coin Metrics' free Community tier actually cover BNB for MVRV/active-addresses/exchange-flows, the way `05_Product_Roadmap.md` asserts? | **Not yet — it's unconfirmed by any source I fetched.** My hypothesis: BNB coverage is inconsistent (likely FREE for active addresses, likely NO-METRIC or PAID for MVRV/flows, since BNB is a newer chain to most on-chain vendors), and this needs the exact live per-metric probe R2 already ran on SOL | If wrong and BNB is fully free: no harm, just extra confirmation work. If wrong the other way (assumed free, actually paid/no-metric) and this ships unverified: the exact fabrication mode this PRD exists to prevent — BNB cells silently rendering a wrong absence class or a paywalled value as free |
| Should SOL network activity use Helius or QuickNode? | **Helius** — its rate-limit docs are explicit and current (10 req/s, 1M credits/mo), while QuickNode's free-tier numbers were only found via a secondary aggregator page, not QuickNode's own docs, in this pass | If wrong: minor — both are free-tier viable per R8; switching later costs one story's worth of rework, not an architectural change |
| Is the "vote program instruction inspection" classification technique (filtering by `Vote111...` program ID) actually the correct, current way to distinguish vote vs. non-vote transactions? | **Probably yes, but UNVERIFIED by this research pass** — it is my own recall, not a fetched source | If wrong: the entire SOL network-activity number is silently mis-computed at the classification layer, which is exactly the kind of confident-wrong number this PRD's SOL exchange-flow exclusion was designed to avoid for a *different* metric — this needs a dedicated, cited confirmation pass before it becomes a story's acceptance criterion, not an assumption baked into `30-spec.md` |

## Blind spots

1. **The vote-filter myth could already be baked into a story's acceptance criteria before anyone notices it's wrong.** The brief itself asked to "confirm the RPC-level filter works as documented" — but no such filter was ever documented, only requested and rejected. If `30-spec.md` is drafted from the brief's framing without reading this document, a story could be written expecting a `votes: false` parameter that has never existed, guaranteeing an implementer attempt burns itself against a nonexistent API surface — precisely the "tripwire fires identically every attempt" failure mode already logged for this project.
2. **Validators.app's mandatory account/token requirement is a provisioning dependency the brief characterized as frictionless ("confirmed genuinely free, no paid tier exists at all").** Free and frictionless are not the same thing — someone has to create an account, generate a token, and store it as a GitHub secret before the first SOL-staking story can even attempt a live call. If that provisioning step isn't scheduled as its own explicit prerequisite, a story will fail on missing credentials and look like a code defect.
3. **Nobody has re-run R2's exact live BNB probe in this research pass.** This document flags the gap honestly, but the risk is that the gap gets treated as "researched" simply because this document exists and discusses BNB at length — it does not contain a single fetched number confirming or denying BNB coverage. If `20-decisions.yaml` is written from this document's prose without someone actually running the probe, BNB coverage becomes exactly the kind of catalog-page assumption R2 explicitly warned against.

## Sources

- https://gitbook-docs.coinmetrics.io/packages/coin-metrics-community-data
- https://gitbook-docs.coinmetrics.io/network-data/network-data-overview/addresses/active-addresses
- https://github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/29856

# 11 · Data model

The compact, authoritative design. Distilled from `research/R5-data-integrity-engineering.md`
and `research/R0-lessons-from-prior-system.md` so stories can inline this instead of the full
research. Where this conflicts with a research file, **this file wins** — it is the decision.

---

## The one rule

**A wrong number must look different from a right one.** Everything below exists to make that
structurally true rather than a matter of discipline.

## 1. Status is a type, not a convention

Four outcomes, modelled as a discriminated union of frozen dataclasses — never one class with
optional fields:

```
Ok(value, source_timestamp)          # we have it, and it is current
Stale(value, source_timestamp)       # we have it, but it is past its freshness budget
Unavailable(reason)                  # we do not have it, and here is why
Error(reason, detail)                # the attempt failed
```

`Unavailable` and `Error` **have no `value` attribute at all**. Reading one is an
`AttributeError`, not a zero.

**Forbidden:** any helper that converts absence back to a number — `.value_or(0.0)`,
`.as_float()`, `or 0`, `fillna(0)`, a neutral default. This is the exact mechanism by which
the prior system's funding rate, open interest and long/short ratio reported a confident
`0.0` for months because a fetcher was never called.

### 1.1 Three kinds of absence, kept distinct

```
NOT_DEFINABLE   the metric has no meaning on this chain and never will
                (SOPR/MVRV on Solana: account-based, no UTXO to timestamp).
                Not purchasable at any price. Permanent, and correct.
PAYWALLED       exists, we lack credentials (realized cap on Coin Metrics free)
FETCH_FAILED    should exist, did not arrive — timeout, 500, empty after filtering
NOT_FETCHED     the pipeline never attempted it
```

`NOT_FETCHED` is the default state of every indicator at the start of a run. It exists so that
"never ran" and "ran and got nothing" are different rows. Collapsing these four into one blank
cell destroys the information the owner most needs: whether a gap is permanent, purchasable,
broken, or a bug.

## 2. Schema

```sql
CREATE TYPE datapoint_status  AS ENUM ('OK','STALE','UNAVAILABLE','ERROR');
CREATE TYPE unavailable_reason AS ENUM ('NOT_DEFINABLE','PAYWALLED','FETCH_FAILED','NOT_FETCHED');

CREATE TABLE datapoints (
  id               bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
  indicator_key    text NOT NULL,          -- FK in spirit to the registry
  asset            text NOT NULL,          -- what we DISPLAY it as
  measured_on      text NOT NULL,          -- what it was ACTUALLY measured on
  value            double precision,       -- NULL unless status IN ('OK','STALE')
  status           datapoint_status NOT NULL,
  reason           unavailable_reason,
  source_vendor    text NOT NULL,
  endpoint         text NOT NULL,
  source_field     text NOT NULL,          -- WHICH FIELD of the response
  fetched_at       timestamptz NOT NULL,   -- when WE fetched
  source_timestamp timestamptz,            -- when the SOURCE says it is as-of
  CONSTRAINT asset_match     CHECK (status <> 'OK' OR measured_on = asset),
  CONSTRAINT value_iff_ok    CHECK ((status IN ('OK','STALE')) = (value IS NOT NULL)),
  CONSTRAINT reason_required CHECK ((status IN ('UNAVAILABLE','ERROR')) = (reason IS NOT NULL))
);

CREATE INDEX ON datapoints (indicator_key, asset, fetched_at DESC);
```

**Long and narrow, never wide.** The prior system stored one column pair per indicator
(`ls_ratio_score`, `oi_raw`, …), so adding an indicator required a migration and its integrity
check covered exactly two hardcoded rows while drifting from reality unnoticed. Here a new
indicator is a row.

### Why each constraint exists

| Constraint | Prevents |
|---|---|
| `asset_match` | BTC's MVRV displayed as SOL's. The prior system did this to 8 coins and called the result *"not degraded data, wrong data"*. Now a **database error** |
| `value_iff_ok` | Status and value drifting apart — a value with no status, or an `OK` with nothing in it |
| `reason_required` | Absence that does not say why |

A mismatched row **may** be inserted as `UNAVAILABLE` for audit. The constraint only forbids
it carrying `OK`. Recording that we fetched the wrong thing is useful; displaying it as
correct is not.

### Two timestamps, two owners

`fetched_at` is set by the **writer**. `source_timestamp` is set by the **fetcher**, from the
source's own as-of time. They answer different questions and must never be conflated.

**A `source_timestamp` in the future is an error, not a value.** The prior system read funding
from `premiumIndex.lastFundingRate` — a continuously-moving estimate for an *upcoming*
settlement — instead of the settled series, and stored it as history. Measured: `0.00002925`
against a settled `0.00003113`, on a number that keeps drifting. This assertion is what makes
that class of bug impossible.

## 3. Registry — one declarative source of truth

```yaml
- key: btc_daily_close
  vendor: okx
  endpoint: https://www.okx.com/api/v5/market/candles?instId=BTC-USDT&bar=1D
  source_field: 'candle[4] (close), where candle[8] == "1"'
  definable_for: [BTC]
  expected_update_interval_seconds: 86400
  freshness_warn_seconds:  108000   # 30h
  freshness_stale_seconds: 172800   # 48h
```

- **`source_field` is mandatory.** Recording only the endpoint is how the funding-rate bug
  stayed invisible — right endpoint, wrong field.
- **`definable_for` is about meaning, not availability**, and a wildcard is rejected. An
  indicator must state which assets it is genuinely valid for.
- Integrity coverage is **generated from this registry**, so an indicator with no coverage is
  a build error rather than an oversight.
- The registry is blast-radius: changing an entry retroactively changes the meaning of every
  stored value carrying that key.

## 4. Freshness — three numbers, not one

| Field | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| `expected_update_interval` | how often the source *publishes* |
| `freshness_warn` | when to flag it visually (≈1.5× interval) |
| `freshness_stale` | when it becomes `STALE` (≈2× interval) |

Two thresholds survive one missed cycle without crying wolf, and catch two. A daily-close
indicator: interval 24h, warn 30h, stale 48h.

**Frozen is a separate check.** A source can be *fresh* — `fetched_at` seconds ago — while
returning an identical payload forever. Detecting that means comparing against the last N
stored values, and it is PRD-009. PRD-001 only provides the columns that make it possible.

## 4b. Reference period vs published date

**The timestamp a value describes is not the timestamp at which it became knowable.** Measured
against the live FRED API on 2026-09-08:

| Series | Latest observation | Days behind that day |
|---|---|---|
| `DFF` (Fed funds) | 2026-09-03 | 5 |
| `DTWEXBGS` (broad USD) | 2026-08-28 | 11 |
| `M2SL` (M2) | 2026-07-01 | **69** |

`M2SL` is a *monthly* series: the July figure is the newest that exists, and it was published
weeks after July ended. Displaying `23218` as today's M2 is false in two separate ways — wrong
period, and silent about the delay.

So a lagged indicator carries **two** timestamps, not one:

- `reference_period` — the period the value describes (July 2026)
- `source_timestamp` / `published_at` — when it became knowable

The UI shows both, and the freshness budget is computed against **publication**, not the
reference period — otherwise every monthly series is permanently `STALE` by construction.

This generalises past macro: funding rate (settled vs predicted), ETF flows (T+1), an unclosed
daily candle, and CPI are all the same shape. `ai-hedge-fund` reached it independently and
enforces it by filtering on `filing_date` rather than `report_period`, because the latter
"leaks 3-6 weeks of future" (R9 §2).

## 4c. Corroboration — disagreement is a finding, not a problem to resolve

Every other rule in this document defends against a failure someone predicted. Corroboration is
the only one that catches a wrong number **nobody thought to check for**, and it is therefore
the most valuable single mechanism here. Designed in PRD-003.

The shape: fetch the same quantity from two or more independent venues, compare, and record the
comparison.

**The trap to avoid:** silently picking a winner. Averaging two disagreeing sources, or
preferring the "primary" one, throws away the only signal that something is wrong and produces
a confident number — which is exactly the failure mode this product exists to eliminate. If two
venues disagree beyond tolerance, **that is the finding**, and it must reach the face of the
value.

Concretely:

- The measured OKX case is the worked example. `bar=1D` (Hong Kong day) gave **78,834.1**;
  `bar=1Dutc` gave **79,111.8** — 0.35% apart. Comparing OKX against Coinbase would have
  flagged it automatically on day one. Instead it was caught because a person read the
  timestamp. That is not a repeatable defence.
- Tolerance is per-indicator and belongs in the registry, not hardcoded. Spot close across major
  venues sits far tighter than, say, aggregated open interest. R5 flagged a specific numeric
  tolerance as **UNVERIFIED** — it must be measured from observed spreads, not guessed.
- Divergence needs its own visible state. Whether that is a new `reason` value, a separate
  `corroboration` column, or a companion row is a PRD-003 decision; what is settled here is that
  it may not be silently swallowed, and that a corroborated value and an uncorroborated one must
  not look identical.
- Corroboration is not available for everything. A metric published by exactly one vendor
  (Coin Metrics MVRV) has no second opinion, and that fact should itself be visible rather than
  implied.

## 4d. Warm-up: measured, not assumed

**A recursive indicator's value depends on how much history preceded it.** Measured 2026-09-10
on 599 real OKX BTC daily closes — the *same final bar*, RSI(14), varying only the length of
history supplied:

| bars supplied | RSI(14) | drift vs converged |
|---|---|---|
| 15 | 47.56 | −11.94 |
| 20 | 48.62 | −10.88 |
| 30 | **63.90** | **+4.40** |
| 50 | 58.98 | −0.52 |
| 100 | 59.51 | +0.008 |
| 150 → 500 | **59.4972** | **0.0000** |

A **16-point spread on a 0–100 oscillator** — the difference between reading oversold and
overbought — with no error, no NaN and a plausible number at every length. This is the prior
system's *"same market, different score"* reproduced exactly, in TA-Lib.

**Two traps this exposes:**

1. **TA-Lib's own `lookback` is not a warm-up figure.** It reports RSI 14, ATR 14, MACD 33,
   STOCHRSI 20, EMA(200) 199. Those are the *mechanical floor* — the inputs consumed before any
   output exists. Taking them as `required_bars` gives RSI 14 bars and a value 12 points wrong.
2. **The unstable period defaults to 0**, so TA-Lib strips nothing and warns nothing. A 30-bar
   RSI array returns a confident float at index 14.

**Therefore:** recursive indicators (RSI, ATR, EMA, StochRSI, **and MACD**, which TA-Lib does
*not* annotate despite its EMA-26 core) declare **250 bars**. Convergence arrives near 150 in
this measurement; 250 is deliberate headroom. Non-recursive indicators (Bollinger, OBV) declare
their own smaller honest N.

The exactly-N contract from PRD-002 is what makes this safe: a cache growing from 30 bars to 150
would otherwise walk RSI from 63.9 to 59.5 over weeks, silently.

## 5. Fallbacks are different indicators

If a value cannot be obtained from its declared source, the answer is `UNAVAILABLE` — **not a
substitute source under the same label.** The prior system silently swapped FRED's `DTWEXBGS`
(26 currencies, weekly, lagged) for yfinance's `DX-Y.NYB` (6 currencies, real-time) behind one
"DXY" label; the value jumped discontinuously whenever the fallback engaged and nothing
recorded which had produced it.

A second source is a second registry entry with its own key, displayed as its own series, or
it does not exist.

## 6. Rendering

TypeScript mirrors the union, with an exhaustive `switch` and a `never` fallthrough so an
unhandled status is a **compile error**:

```ts
type Datapoint =
  | { status: "OK";          value: number; sourceTimestamp: string }
  | { status: "STALE";       value: number; sourceTimestamp: string }
  | { status: "UNAVAILABLE"; reason: Reason }
  | { status: "ERROR";       reason: Reason; detail: string };
```

- `UNAVAILABLE` renders an em dash and its reason. **Never `0`. Never blank.**
- `STALE` renders the value **with its age and a visible stale treatment** — shown, but never
  shown as if current.
- Provenance (vendor, endpoint, source timestamp) is on the face of the value, not behind a
  click.
- No "last known good" fallback that silently presents an older value as current.

# Databases

> A database is the persistent store behind any website or app: it holds users, content, orders, sessions, and (increasingly) the embeddings that power AI features. Choosing one matters more in the AI era because modern apps usually need **two storage shapes at once**: a transactional/relational store for app state (users, billing, content) and a **vector store** for semantic search and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). # Mobile & PWA

> Mobile & PWA is the layer that extends a web product onto phones and tablets, either by making your existing site installable and offline-capable (a Progressive Web App) or by shipping a real app to the Apple App Store and Google Play built from a shared codebase (React Native, Expo, Flutter, Capacitor, etc.). The cheapest path that meets your requirements wins.

# crypto-data-live-platform

<!--
Written by a person, kept short. Generated agent instructions measurably do not help —
they cost tokens on every invocation and slightly reduce success rates, while
human-written context improves them. When an agent learns something worth keeping it
writes a proposal to `.uf/proposals/`; you fold in the ones that are actually true.

An empty section is better than an invented one.
-->

**Stack:** Python 3.12 (`uv`, httpx, pydantic, TA-Lib) ingestion · Supabase Postgres ·
Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind on Cloudflare Pages, behind Cloudflare Access ·
GitHub Actions `schedule:` + cron-job.org `repository_dispatch` triggers ·
Healthchecks.io dead-man's-switch.
See `project-documents/10_Technical_Architecture.md`.

> **Compute location is UNDECIDED** until PRD-001's reachability spike runs. Binance returns
> HTTP 451 to US IPs, which is what forced the prior system onto a self-hosted runner that
> later died silently. Do not assume GitHub-hosted runners can reach every venue — measure it.

**This product's one rule above all others:** it displays market data and **makes no
judgement about it**. No composite score, no signal, no ranking. A wrong number must look
different from a right one — that is the whole product. If a value cannot be honestly sourced
for an asset, it renders `UNAVAILABLE` with a reason, never a proxy and never `0`.

## How work happens here

This product runs on `uf`. Read `CYCLE.md` for the loop, `SKILLS.md` for which skill to fire
at which phase, `KNOWLEDGE.md` for what we already know.

Work is organised as **PRDs** in `prds/PRD-00N-<slug>/`, walked in the order set by
`project-documents/05_Product_Roadmap.md`. Each PRD compiles to `spec.lock.json`, then runs
story by story: one agent implements in a fresh context, a **different vendor** verifies in
a read-only sandbox and must cite a file, line or test name per criterion.

**You cannot mark your own work complete.** Produce the evidence the criteria name — the
tests, the screenshots, the passing commands — and leave it where it can be found. Do not
write a summary claiming success; nobody reads it and the verifier ignores it.

## Conventions

<!-- Add the real ones as you discover them. -->

## Gotchas

<!-- Things that cost an afternoon. Also run `uf learn` so other products inherit them. -->

## Blast radius

Changes to these need human review before merge (mirrored in `.uf/config.json`):

- authentication and session handling
- RLS policies
- payments
- database migrations
- CI workflows and deploy configuration

## What we already knew, and whether it still holds

| Claim from our knowledge base | Still true? | What the source says | Citation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coin Metrics free Community API needs no API key | **Confirmed** | Community endpoints at `api.coinmetrics.io/v4` require no key | [gitbook-docs.coinmetrics.io/access-our-data/api](https://gitbook-docs.coinmetrics.io/access-our-data/api), confirmed on [coin-metrics-community-data](https://gitbook-docs.coinmetrics.io/packages/coin-metrics-community-data) |
| R2's live probe found BTC/ETH MVRV, active addresses, exchange flows FREE; SOL MVRV/exchange-flows NO-METRIC | Holds — not contradicted by anything fetched | No public source disputes R2's live probe; Coin Metrics' own coverage explorer is the only way to re-verify, and it requires a live query per asset/metric, which is what R2 already did | Not independently re-verified here — see Open Questions |
| "Coin Metrics API key provisioning and rate limits... need confirming" (brief's open question) | **Now answered** | Community tier: **10 requests / 6-second sliding window per IP (~1.6 req/s)**, no key required | [coinmetrics.readthedocs.io/en/latest/community.html](https://coinmetrics.readthedocs.io/en/latest/community.html) via search, corroborated by [gitbook-docs.coinmetrics.io/access-our-data/api](https://gitbook-docs.coinmetrics.io/access-our-data/api) |
| "BNB coverage is asserted in the roadmap but not independently confirmed" (brief's open question) | **Still unconfirmed** | Neither Coin Metrics doc fetched lists per-asset metric coverage inline; the actual answer lives behind a live query to `coverage.coinmetrics.io` or the `/v4/catalog-all/asset-metrics` endpoint, which this research pass did not execute against BNB specifically | [gitbook-docs.coinmetrics.io/network-data/network-data-overview/addresses/active-addresses](https://gitbook-docs.coinmetrics.io/network-data/network-data-overview/addresses/active-addresses) confirms only that privacy coins (Monero, Grin) are excluded — silent on BNB either way |
| R8: "Vote vs. non-vote transaction filtering on Solana... could not reconfirm the current vote/non-vote split live" | **R8 was right to flag this — and the answer is worse than "unconfirmed": it's unsupported** | `getBlock`'s only config params are `commitment`, `encoding`, `transactionDetails`, `maxSupportedTransactionVersion`, `rewards` — **no vote-filter parameter exists**. A 2022 feature request to add one (`votes: bool`) was explicitly closed as **not planned** | [solana.com/docs/rpc/http/getblock](https://solana.com/docs/rpc/http/getblock); [github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/29856](https://github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/29856) (closed, not planned; repo itself now archived) |
| R8: Validators.app "confirmed genuinely free, no paid tier exists at all" | **Holds, but with a real constraint not previously recorded** | No paid tier is documented, but the free API is rate-limited to **20 or 40 requests per 5 minutes depending on endpoint**, requires a verified account + token, and returns 429 on overage | [validators.app/api-documentation](https://www.validators.app/api-documentation) |
| R8: Helius/QuickNode "both confirmed free tiers... neither was load-tested" | **Partially updated** | Helius free tier: **1M monthly credits, 10 req/s** overall cap, with tighter per-method sub-limits (1 `sendTransaction`/s, 2 DAS calls/s, 5 `getProgramAccounts`/s) — this project's read-only daily batch (getBlock/getSignaturesForAddress calls) fits comfortably under 10 req/s if paced | [helius.dev/docs/billing/rate-limits](https://www.helius.dev/docs/billing/rate-limits) |

## Existing implementations

Real dashboards separate the exact three metric classes this PRD does:

- **The Block** and **Token Terminal** both publish "Non-vote transactions on Solana" as a distinct series from raw transaction count, precisely because raw counts are consensus noise, not user activity — both are downstream evidence that shipped implementations treat vote-filtering as necessary, even though the raw RPC gives no server-side lever for it: [theblock.co/data/on-chain-metrics/solana/non-vote-transactions-on-the-solana-network-daily-7dma](https://www.theblock.co/data/on-chain-metrics/solana/non-vote-transactions-on-the-solana-network-daily-7dma), [tokenterminal.com/explorer/projects/solana/metrics/non-vote-transaction-count](https://tokenterminal.com/explorer/projects/solana/metrics/non-vote-transaction-count).
- **Solscan's own analytics dashboard** exposes "vote vs non-vote transactions" as a first-class split view, again implying client-side classification against fetched blocks rather than a filtered RPC call: [analytics.solscan.io/overview/transaction/vote-vs-non-vote-trans](https://analytics.solscan.io/overview/transaction/vote-vs-non-vote-trans).
- **UNVERIFIED** (own recall, not confirmed by a fetched source this pass): the standard client-side technique is to inspect each transaction's account keys / program invocations for the vote program address `Vote111111111111111111111111111111111111111` and classify a transaction as a vote iff every top-level instruction targets that program. This needs direct confirmation against Solana's program docs or a working reference implementation before it becomes a story's acceptance criterion — flagged as a research gap below, not a settled fact.
- **Coin Metrics' own Python/R clients** (`coinmetrics-api-client`) wrap the same public `/v4` community endpoints this PRD would call directly via httpx — evidence the free tier is treated as production-usable by Coin Metrics itself, not a crippled trial: [github.com/coinmetrics/docs-website](https://github.com/coinmetrics/docs-website).

## Approach options

**1. Coin Metrics Community API, direct httpx, for BTC/ETH (and BNB if confirmed) — recommended for the on-chain fetch.**
How: daily batch call to `/v4/timeseries/asset-metrics` for `CapMVRVCur`, `AdrActCnt`, exchange-flow metrics, one asset per call to respect the ~1.6 req/s ceiling. Cost: $0. Trade-off: rate limit means a 4-asset × 3-metric daily batch (12 calls) takes ~7+ seconds minimum if serialized correctly — trivial for a once-daily job, but a naive concurrent implementation will get 429'd. Who uses it: Coin Metrics' own community client library is built on exactly this endpoint set ([github.com/coinmetrics/docs-website](https://github.com/coinmetrics/docs-website)).

**2. Helius free-tier RPC for SOL network activity — recommended for the build side.**
How: `getBlock` per slot (or `getSignaturesForAddress`/batch RPC) at a sampled cadence, client-side vote-filtering, aggregated to daily non-vote tx count + unique signers. Cost: $0 within 1M credits/mo, 10 req/s ceiling ([helius.dev/docs/billing/rate-limits](https://www.helius.dev/docs/billing/rate-limits)). Trade-off: no server-side vote filter exists at all ([github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/29856](https://github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/29856)) — every block's full transaction list must be pulled and filtered locally, which is real client-side compute and credit cost, not "free" in the way R8 characterized it.

**3. QuickNode free tier as the Solana RPC alternative.**
How: same interface as Helius, different provider. Trade-off: R8 did not load-test either against this project's real batch shape, and this research pass did not re-test it either — this remains a genuine open decision, not a settled one. Cost: $0 documented free tier exists, per [quicknode.com/builders-guide/best/top-10-free-rpc-endpoints-for-developers](https://www.quicknode.com/builders-guide/best/top-10-free-rpc-endpoints-for-developers).

**4. Validators.app for SOL staking/validator data — recommended, only option researched with a confirmed no-paid-tier posture.**
How: token-gated GET requests against their REST API for validator count, commission, active stake. Cost: $0, but capped at 20–40 requests/5 min depending on endpoint, with a mandatory account + API token, not a fully anonymous free tier ([validators.app/api-documentation](https://www.validators.app/api-documentation)) — a materially stricter free tier than Coin Metrics' anonymous-by-IP model.

**Recommendation:** Coin Metrics Community API (option 1) for BTC/ETH/BNB-if-confirmed, Helius free tier (option 2) for SOL network activity, Validators.app (option 4) for SOL staking. This matches R8's build-don't-buy verdict and every number above is now sourced rather than catalog-asserted — one line of justification: **it's the only combination where every claimed "free" limit has a live-fetched number attached to it (rate limit, credit cap, or req/5min cap), not a vendor marketing page.**

## Edge cases and gotchas

- **The vote-filter gotcha is worse than "unconfirmed" — it's a myth to retire.** R8 phrased this as "a filtering problem, not a scale-blocking problem," implying some RPC-level knob exists to flip. It doesn't: `getBlock` has never supported vote exclusion, and the 2022 feature request for it was explicitly rejected ([github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/29856](https://github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/29856)). Any story that says "confirm the RPC-level filter works as documented" is testing something that was never documented to exist. The story needs to specify client-side vote-program-instruction classification instead, and that classification logic itself needs a cited reference before being written into an acceptance criterion — currently it is only this document's UNVERIFIED recall.
- **Coin Metrics' rate limit is per-IP, not per-key** — a GitHub Actions runner's ephemeral IP means the limit resets cleanly run-to-run, but also means it cannot be "banked" or monitored via a dashboard; a burst of concurrent asset/metric calls at the start of a batch job will 429 silently unless serialized with backoff (10 req/6s ≈ 1.6 req/s — [coinmetrics.readthedocs.io/en/latest/community.html](https://coinmetrics.readthedocs.io/en/latest/community.html)).
- **Validators.app requires a verified account and per-endpoint rate ceilings** — this is a materially different trust/provisioning model than Coin Metrics' anonymous-by-IP approach, and the brief's framing of R8's "confirmed genuinely free" undersold the friction: a token must be provisioned and stored as a secret before US-0xx work can even start ([validators.app/api-documentation](https://www.validators.app/api-documentation)).
- **Helius free-tier per-method sub-caps can bite even under the 10 req/s headline number** — `getProgramAccounts` is capped at 5/s and DAS calls at 2/s regardless of the 10 req/s overall ceiling; if the SOL story ends up needing `getProgramAccounts` for anything (e.g. enumerating stake accounts as a cross-check against Validators.app), that path is throttled tighter than the naive "10 req/s, fine" read of the plan ([helius.dev/docs/billing/rate-limits](https://www.helius.dev/docs/billing/rate-limits)).

# 11 · Data model

The compact, authoritative design. Distilled from `research/R5-data-integrity-engineering.md`
and `research/R0-lessons-from-prior-system.md` so stories can inline this instead of the full
research. Where this conflicts with a research file, **this file wins** — it is the decision.

---

## The one rule

**A wrong number must look different from a right one.** Everything below exists to make that
structurally true rather than a matter of discipline.

## 1. Status is a type, not a convention

Four outcomes, modelled as a discriminated union of frozen dataclasses — never one class with
optional fields:

```
Ok(value, source_timestamp)          # we have it, and it is current
Stale(value, source_timestamp)       # we have it, but it is past its freshness budget
Unavailable(reason)                  # we do not have it, and here is why
Error(reason, detail)                # the attempt failed
```

`Unavailable` and `Error` **have no `value` attribute at all**. Reading one is an
`AttributeError`, not a zero.

**Forbidden:** any helper that converts absence back to a number — `.value_or(0.0)`,
`.as_float()`, `or 0`, `fillna(0)`, a neutral default. This is the exact mechanism by which
the prior system's funding rate, open interest and long/short ratio reported a confident
`0.0` for months because a fetcher was never called.

### 1.1 Three kinds of absence, kept distinct

```
NOT_DEFINABLE   the metric has no meaning on this chain and never will
                (SOPR/MVRV on Solana: account-based, no UTXO to timestamp).
                Not purchasable at any price. Permanent, and correct.
PAYWALLED       exists, we lack credentials (realized cap on Coin Metrics free)
FETCH_FAILED    should exist, did not arrive — timeout, 500, empty after filtering
NOT_FETCHED     the pipeline never attempted it
```

`NOT_FETCHED` is the default state of every indicator at the start of a run. It exists so that
"never ran" and "ran and got nothing" are different rows. Collapsing these four into one blank
cell destroys the information the owner most needs: whether a gap is permanent, purchasable,
broken, or a bug.

## 2. Schema

```sql
CREATE TYPE datapoint_status  AS ENUM ('OK','STALE','UNAVAILABLE','ERROR');
CREATE TYPE unavailable_reason AS ENUM ('NOT_DEFINABLE','PAYWALLED','FETCH_FAILED','NOT_FETCHED');

CREATE TABLE datapoints (
  id               bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
  indicator_key    text NOT NULL,          -- FK in spirit to the registry
  asset            text NOT NULL,          -- what we DISPLAY it as
  measured_on      text NOT NULL,          -- what it was ACTUALLY measured on
  value            double precision,       -- NULL unless status IN ('OK','STALE')
  status           datapoint_status NOT NULL,
  reason           unavailable_reason,
  source_vendor    text NOT NULL,
  endpoint         text NOT NULL,
  source_field     text NOT NULL,          -- WHICH FIELD of the response
  fetched_at       timestamptz NOT NULL,   -- when WE fetched
  source_timestamp timestamptz,            -- when the SOURCE says it is as-of
  CONSTRAINT asset_match     CHECK (status <> 'OK' OR measured_on = asset),
  CONSTRAINT value_iff_ok    CHECK ((status IN ('OK','STALE')) = (value IS NOT NULL)),
  CONSTRAINT reason_required CHECK ((status IN ('UNAVAILABLE','ERROR')) = (reason IS NOT NULL))
);

CREATE INDEX ON datapoints (indicator_key, asset, fetched_at DESC);
```

**Long and narrow, never wide.** The prior system stored one column pair per indicator
(`ls_ratio_score`, `oi_raw`, …), so adding an indicator required a migration and its integrity
check covered exactly two hardcoded rows while drifting from reality unnoticed. Here a new
indicator is a row.

### Why each constraint exists

| Constraint | Prevents |
|---|---|
| `asset_match` | BTC's MVRV displayed as SOL's. The prior system did this to 8 coins and called the result *"not degraded data, wrong data"*. Now a **database error** |
| `value_iff_ok` | Status and value drifting apart — a value with no status, or an `OK` with nothing in it |
| `reason_required` | Absence that does not say why |

A mismatched row **may** be inserted as `UNAVAILABLE` for audit. The constraint only forbids
it carrying `OK`. Recording that we fetched the wrong thing is useful; displaying it as
correct is not.

### Two timestamps, two owners

`fetched_at` is set by the **writer**. `source_timestamp` is set by the **fetcher**, from the
source's own as-of time. They answer different questions and must never be conflated.

**A `source_timestamp` in the future is an error, not a value.** The prior system read funding
from `premiumIndex.lastFundingRate` — a continuously-moving estimate for an *upcoming*
settlement — instead of the settled series, and stored it as history. Measured: `0.00002925`
against a settled `0.00003113`, on a number that keeps drifting. This assertion is what makes
that class of bug impossible.

## 3. Registry — one declarative source of truth

```yaml
- key: btc_daily_close
  vendor: okx
  endpoint: https://www.okx.com/api/v5/market/candles?instId=BTC-USDT&bar=1D
  source_field: 'candle[4] (close), where candle[8] == "1"'
  definable_for: [BTC]
  expected_update_interval_seconds: 86400
  freshness_warn_seconds:  108000   # 30h
  freshness_stale_seconds: 172800   # 48h
```

- **`source_field` is mandatory.** Recording only the endpoint is how the funding-rate bug
  stayed invisible — right endpoint, wrong field.
- **`definable_for` is about meaning, not availability**, and a wildcard is rejected. An
  indicator must state which assets it is genuinely valid for.
- Integrity coverage is **generated from this registry**, so an indicator with no coverage is
  a build error rather than an oversight.
- The registry is blast-radius: changing an entry retroactively changes the meaning of every
  stored value carrying that key.

## 4. Freshness — three numbers, not one

| Field | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| `expected_update_interval` | how often the source *publishes* |
| `freshness_warn` | when to flag it visually (≈1.5× interval) |
| `freshness_stale` | when it becomes `STALE` (≈2× interval) |

Two thresholds survive one missed cycle without crying wolf, and catch two. A daily-close
indicator: interval 24h, warn 30h, stale 48h.

**Frozen is a separate check.** A source can be *fresh* — `fetched_at` seconds ago — while
returning an identical payload forever. Detecting that means comparing against the last N
stored values, and it is PRD-009. PRD-001 only provides the columns that make it possible.

## 4b. Reference period vs published date

**The timestamp a value describes is not the timestamp at which it became knowable.** Measured
against the live FRED API on 2026-09-08:

| Series | Latest observation | Days behind that day |
|---|---|---|
| `DFF` (Fed funds) | 2026-09-03 | 5 |
| `DTWEXBGS` (broad USD) | 2026-08-28 | 11 |
| `M2SL` (M2) | 2026-07-01 | **69** |

`M2SL` is a *monthly* series: the July figure is the newest that exists, and it was published
weeks after July ended. Displaying `23218` as today's M2 is false in two separate ways — wrong
period, and silent about the delay.

So a lagged indicator carries **two** timestamps, not one:

- `reference_period` — the period the value describes (July 2026)
- `source_timestamp` / `published_at` — when it became knowable

The UI shows both, and the freshness budget is computed against **publication**, not the
reference period — otherwise every monthly series is permanently `STALE` by construction.

This generalises past macro: funding rate (settled vs predicted), ETF flows (T+1), an unclosed
daily candle, and CPI are all the same shape. `ai-hedge-fund` reached it independently and
enforces it by filtering on `filing_date` rather than `report_period`, because the latter
"leaks 3-6 weeks of future" (R9 §2).

## 4c. Corroboration — disagreement is a finding, not a problem to resolve

Every other rule in this document defends against a failure someone predicted. Corroboration is
the only one that catches a wrong number **nobody thought to check for**, and it is therefore
the most valuable single mechanism here. Designed in PRD-003.

The shape: fetch the same quantity from two or more independent venues, compare, and record the
comparison.

**The trap to avoid:** silently picking a winner. Averaging two disagreeing sources, or
preferring the "primary" one, throws away the only signal that something is wrong and produces
a confident number — which is exactly the failure mode this product exists to eliminate. If two
venues disagree beyond tolerance, **that is the finding**, and it must reach the face of the
value.

Concretely:

- The measured OKX case is the worked example. `bar=1D` (Hong Kong day) gave **78,834.1**;
  `bar=1Dutc` gave **79,111.8** — 0.35% apart. Comparing OKX against Coinbase would have
  flagged it automatically on day one. Instead it was caught because a person read the
  timestamp. That is not a repeatable defence.
- Tolerance is per-indicator and belongs in the registry, not hardcoded. Spot close across major
  venues sits far tighter than, say, aggregated open interest. R5 flagged a specific numeric
  tolerance as **UNVERIFIED** — it must be measured from observed spreads, not guessed.
- Divergence needs its own visible state. Whether that is a new `reason` value, a separate
  `corroboration` column, or a companion row is a PRD-003 decision; what is settled here is that
  it may not be silently swallowed, and that a corroborated value and an uncorroborated one must
  not look identical.
- Corroboration is not available for everything. A metric published by exactly one vendor
  (Coin Metrics MVRV) has no second opinion, and that fact should itself be visible rather than
  implied.

## 4d. Warm-up: measured, not assumed

**A recursive indicator's value depends on how much history preceded it.** Measured 2026-09-10
on 599 real OKX BTC daily closes — the *same final bar*, RSI(14), varying only the length of
history supplied:

| bars supplied | RSI(14) | drift vs converged |
|---|---|---|
| 15 | 47.56 | −11.94 |
| 20 | 48.62 | −10.88 |
| 30 | **63.90** | **+4.40** |
| 50 | 58.98 | −0.52 |
| 100 | 59.51 | +0.008 |
| 150 → 500 | **59.4972** | **0.0000** |

A **16-point spread on a 0–100 oscillator** — the difference between reading oversold and
overbought — with no error, no NaN and a plausible number at every length. This is the prior
system's *"same market, different score"* reproduced exactly, in TA-Lib.

**Two traps this exposes:**

1. **TA-Lib's own `lookback` is not a warm-up figure.** It reports RSI 14, ATR 14, MACD 33,
   STOCHRSI 20, EMA(200) 199. Those are the *mechanical floor* — the inputs consumed before any
   output exists. Taking them as `required_bars` gives RSI 14 bars and a value 12 points wrong.
2. **The unstable period defaults to 0**, so TA-Lib strips nothing and warns nothing. A 30-bar
   RSI array returns a confident float at index 14.

**Therefore:** recursive indicators (RSI, ATR, EMA, StochRSI, **and MACD**, which TA-Lib does
*not* annotate despite its EMA-26 core) declare **250 bars**. Convergence arrives near 150 in
this measurement; 250 is deliberate headroom. Non-recursive indicators (Bollinger, OBV) declare
their own smaller honest N.

The exactly-N contract from PRD-002 is what makes this safe: a cache growing from 30 bars to 150
would otherwise walk RSI from 63.9 to 59.5 over weeks, silently.

## 5. Fallbacks are different indicators

If a value cannot be obtained from its declared source, the answer is `UNAVAILABLE` — **not a
substitute source under the same label.** The prior system silently swapped FRED's `DTWEXBGS`
(26 currencies, weekly, lagged) for yfinance's `DX-Y.NYB` (6 currencies, real-time) behind one
"DXY" label; the value jumped discontinuously whenever the fallback engaged and nothing
recorded which had produced it.

A second source is a second registry entry with its own key, displayed as its own series, or
it does not exist.

## 6. Rendering

TypeScript mirrors the union, with an exhaustive `switch` and a `never` fallthrough so an
unhandled status is a **compile error**:

```ts
type Datapoint =
  | { status: "OK";          value: number; sourceTimestamp: string }
  | { status: "STALE";       value: number; sourceTimestamp: string }
  | { status: "UNAVAILABLE"; reason: Reason }
  | { status: "ERROR";       reason: Reason; detail: string };
```

- `UNAVAILABLE` renders an em dash and its reason. **Never `0`. Never blank.**
- `STALE` renders the value **with its age and a visible stale treatment** — shown, but never
  shown as if current.
- Provenance (vendor, endpoint, source timestamp) is on the face of the value, not behind a
  click.
- No "last known good" fallback that silently presents an older value as current.

# Payments & Billing

> Payments and billing is how your product collects money: a one-time charge, a recurring subscription, a marketplace payout, or a usage-based invoice. The stack splits into a few jobs: the **payment gateway/processor** (charges the card - Stripe, Adyen, Square), the **Merchant of Record (MoR)** that becomes the legal seller and handles global sales tax/VAT for you (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy), the **billing/subscription engine** that manages plans, proration, dunning, and invoicing (Stripe Billing, Chargebee, Recurly), and **fraud/tax** tooling layered on top. In the AI era, agents increasingly create checkout sessions, manage subscriptions, and reconcile invoices via API, plus emerging "agentic commerce" rails let agents pay on a user's behalf - so clean APIs, idempotency, and webhook-driven state are essential.

This document is technology-agnostic. The central decision is **gateway vs Merchant of Record**: a gateway is cheaper per transaction but you own tax compliance and chargebacks; an MoR costs more but eliminates global tax filing and absorbs chargebacks. **All prices are USD and current as of June 2026; verify on vendor pricing pages before committing.**

# Databases

> A database is the persistent store behind any website or app: it holds users, content, orders, sessions, and (increasingly) the embeddings that power AI features. Choosing one matters more in the AI era because modern apps usually need **two storage shapes at once**: a transactional/relational store for app state (users, billing, content) and a **vector store** for semantic search and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). The cheapest, lowest-friction path for most teams in 2025-2026 is a managed **Postgres** that also speaks vectors (via `pgvector`), so a single database covers both relational and AI workloads until scale forces specialization. Pricing models vary wildly (flat tier vs. usage-based vs. per-row-read), and the real bill is usually driven by hidden levers, egress, row reads, idle/always-on compute, and backup retention, not the headline sticker price. This guide is technology-agnostic and optimizes for cost at each scale tier.

---

| **Small / SMB** (hobby, MVP, < ~50K MAU) | **Supabase** (Free → Pro) or **Neon** (Free → Launch) | Postgres + Auth + Storage + `pgvector` in one. Generous free tiers; Neon's scale-to-zero is near-free for bursty/idle workloads. Single DB handles relational + AI. | $0 (free tier) → **$25–50** |
| **Medium** (funded startup, real traffic, compliance starting) | **Neon Scale** or **Supabase Pro + compute add-ons**; pair with **Upstash Redis** (cache) and keep vectors in `pgvector` or **Qdrant Cloud** | Predictable Postgres with branching/PITR, managed pooling, room to grow. Add a dedicated vector DB only past ~1M vectors. | **$100–600** |
| **Large / Enterprise** (HA, compliance, high QPS, big data) | **AWS Aurora** (or **Cloud SQL**) for OLTP + **Pinecone**/**Qdrant** for vectors + **ClickHouse Cloud**/**BigQuery**/**Snowflake** for analytics | Battle-tested HA, SLAs, SOC2/HIPAA, multi-AZ. Separate OLTP, vector, and OLAP for performance isolation. | **$1,500 – $20,000+** |

> Rule of thumb: **Start on one managed Postgres with `pgvector`. Add Redis for caching, a dedicated vector DB past ~1M vectors, and a separate OLAP warehouse only when analytics queries start hurting your transactional DB.**

# crypto-data-live-platform

<!--
Written by a person, kept short. Generated agent instructions measurably do not help —
they cost tokens on every invocation and slightly reduce success rates, while
human-written context improves them. When an agent learns something worth keeping it
writes a proposal to `.uf/proposals/`; you fold in the ones that are actually true.
